Shipped `tag`: zero-shot semantic tagging, printing {embedder: {tag: score}},
top-k per embedder (-k, default 3), recomputed each run, never persisted.
Candidate domain = 1/2/3 n-phrases mined corpus-wide, so a todo can get a
phrase it never uses. Added n-phrase chunking (one vector per window) to the
embed write path. Extracted shared _refresh_embeddings/_load_corpus/
_resolve_embedders and made them read corpus + vectors through the store
(inline vectors, backend-agnostic), so search AND tag now work on the

embeddings (backfill-empty, trust-existing, tolerant of an unavailable
backend). 150 tests pass, including JSON-backend tag and doctor-refresh
coverage. Kept it simple per the plan: no hubness correction, no linguistic
pruning (noted as future work).

Body.raw:
Zero-shot ("one-shot") semantic tagging for todos: tag each todo with phrases
drawn from a corpus-wide candidate domain, scored by embedding cosine, keeping
the top k (3). Spec source: /tmp/foo ("Managing embeddings" + "Managing tags").

VERDICT (verified 2026-08-04): the tagging MACHINERY works end to end and is
well covered by tests. The SEMANTIC property does NOT hold in the shipped path:
automatic tags are computed with the `hash` embedder, which is bag-of-words
hashing (lexical), so the spec's motivating case scores exactly 0.0 and the
emitted tags are hash-collision noise. Evidence and repro below.

=== WHERE THE CODE LIVES NOW (read this first) ===

NOT on branch ef4ad78d-zero-shot-semantic-tagg. That branch and its worktree
were deleted after the work was PORTED into master. The port is explicit in the
source: several docstrings read "Ported from ef4ad78d's zero-shot tagger".

Live implementation, master (d06f94c at time of writing),
skills/projectmanagement/todos/todo.py:

  _split_phrases            :436   phrase split (sentence terminators, newlines)
  _nphrase_windows          :445   contiguous 1..3 phrase windows (_MAX_NPHRASE=3 :427)
  _load_corpus              :999   all tickets + Summary/Body raw, via the store
  _mine_tag_candidates      :1029  deduped downcased union of n-phrases = tag domain
  compute_auto_tags         :1050  embed text + candidates, cosine, top-k (_AUTO_TAG_K=3 :994)
  _recompute_auto_tags      :3687  trust-existing / backfill-empty; called by _doctor_one :3743
  _drop_stale_automatic_tags:662   drops auto tags when raw text changes; called on write :718
  tag_findings              :968   doctor validation of Tag shape
  apply_tag_add/_remove     :919/:941  manual tags (CLI: tagadd / tagrm, set --tag/--untag)

Schema actually used: top-level "Tag": [{"raw": <str>, "manual": <bool>}, ...].
Automatic elements are manual:false; manual ones are always preserved.

Original branch commits are dangling but still resolvable at time of writing
(they will be garbage-collected eventually): 0a4e98e init, 7c0febd WI1 end test,
c86482a WI2 splitter, 13618d5 WI3 chunking, 968803e WI4 shared refresh,
4377b85 WI5 mining, c6e8821 WI6 tag core, d97acf5 WI7 tag CLI,
0717349 WI8 store abstraction, b383d07 WI8 doctor+docs, 3df3b3d done.

=== HOW TO VERIFY (reproducible) ===

  cd ~/github.com/jovlinger/utils/skills/projectmanagement/todos

  # 1. test coverage of the tag feature
  pytest test_todo_tag.py test_todo_tag_impl.py -q     # observed: 59 passed
  pytest test_todo.py -k "Tag or tag" -q               # observed: 8 passed

  # 2. end-to-end on the real corpus: doctor recomputes automatic tags
  ./todo.py doctor ef4ad78d | jq -c '{ok, auto_tags}'
  ./todo.py read ef4ad78d  | jq -c '[.Tag[] | {raw, manual}]'

Observed 2026-08-04 on the real store
(~/github.com/jovlinger/utils/.todo/storage), from a todo with no Tag field:
doctor returned {"ok":true,"auto_tags":3} and wrote three manual:false Tag
elements. Re-running doctor is a cheap no-op (existing automatic tags are
trusted). Editing Summary/Body drops the automatic tags (verified: after a
--body edit the Tag field disappeared), and the next doctor run recomputes them.

So the LOOP works: mine -> embed -> cosine -> top-k -> persist -> invalidate.

  # 3. is it actually SEMANTIC? (the probe that matters)
  # Doc about testing that never contains the word "testing"; candidates
  # ["testing","database migration","user interface","deployment"]; score each
  # with todo_embed.cosine_similarity(embed(doc), embed(candidate)).
  # DOC = "Write pytest cases for the parser. Cover edge conditions and assert
  #        the expected output. Run the suite in CI before merging."

Observed 2026-08-04:

  hash  (cheap; THE ONE AUTO-TAGS USE)     apple (semantic; never used)
    +0.1313  user interface                  +0.7823  deployment
    +0.0000  testing                         +0.6951  testing
    +0.0000  database migration              +0.6535  user interface
    +0.0000  deployment                      +0.6460  database migration
    winner: "user interface"                 winner: "deployment"

Reading: with `hash`, "testing" scores EXACTLY 0.0 (no shared tokens -- it is
128-bucket md5 bag-of-words, so unrelated text can only match by collision) and
the winner is noise. The spec's whole motivating case -- tag a document about
testing with "testing" even though the word never appears -- fails outright.
With `apple` the scores are semantic (testing 0.70 >> 0), but raw top-k still
picks "deployment": every candidate sits at 0.64-0.78, the classic hubness
problem, which the design called for fixing with a per-candidate z-score that
was never implemented.

This also explains the live tags on this very todo: they are long fragments
mined from an UNRELATED todo (about "relationship kinds"), i.e. collision noise,
not topicality.

=== SPEC CONFORMANCE ===

Managing embeddings:
1. Refresh fn for all todos, invoked by search and by tagging, default=all
   embedders -- PARTIAL. Search has lazy backfill (todo.py:1568-1582) and the
   auto-tag path trusts/backfills too, but they are separate code paths: the
   shared _refresh_embeddings extracted on the original branch was not carried
   into the port. The tag path uses cheap_embedders()[0] only (:3714-3718).
2. Updating a field zeroes its embedding -- DONE (:662, :718).
3. Search trusts existing vectors, recomputes only empties -- DONE (:1568-1582);
   auto tags follow the same policy (:3701).
4. Embed 1,2,3 n-phrases for each embeddable location (Summary, Body) -- DONE
   (_nphrase_windows + _EMBED_FIELDS).

Managing tags:
1. Zero-shot SEMANTIC tagging -- MECHANISM DONE, SEMANTICS NOT DELIVERED. See
   the probe above: the shipped path runs on `hash` (lexical). `apple` is
   registered but is not "cheap", so _recompute_auto_tags never selects it.
2. Domain = 1,2,3-grams from the whole corpus, pruning optional -- DEVIATION.
   The domain is 1..3 *n-phrases* (sentence-scale windows), not word n-grams, so
   tags are sentence-length fragments rather than keywords. No pruning (allowed).
3. Store as {embedder: {tag: score}}, separate top-k per embedder -- DEVIATION.
   Stored as a flat "Tag" list of {raw, manual}: no score, no per-embedder
   bucketing, single embedder. Documented in the compute_auto_tags docstring.
4. Tags NOT persisted durably, recomputed each run -- DEVIATION. Automatic tags
   ARE persisted by doctor and then trusted; invalidation is by raw-text change
   rather than recomputation every run.
5. Mostly programmatic, no agent intervention -- DONE.

=== FOLLOW-UPS (in priority order) ===

1. Use a semantic embedder for auto tags. Either mark apple cheap-enough for
   this path or let _recompute_auto_tags pick the best AVAILABLE embedder.
   Without this the feature is lexical and the "semantic" name is wrong.
2. Add the hubness correction (per-candidate z-score across the corpus) before
   top-k. The apple column above shows raw cosine alone picks the wrong tag.
3. Mine word-level n-grams (1-3 words) so tags are keywords, not sentences.
4. Restore per-embedder tag buckets with scores if cross-embedder comparison is
   still wanted (spec item 3); note scores are not comparable across embedders.
